title: Restrictive employment covenants
summary: A noncompetition covenant limits a worker’s or business seller’s ability to compete after a relationship ends. Its enforceability requires the particular governing restrictions and the scope of the restraint to be examined.
notes:
Hassler analyzes the employer’s asserted interests, the duration and geography of the restraint, and the court’s approach to overbreadth. The consequences of an excessive clause may differ depending on whether the governing law permits partial enforcement or rewriting. An agreement supported by consideration and signed voluntarily can still encounter these limits.

The Fall 2026 supplement separately reproduces federal materials removing an FTC rule after litigation. They are a specific source history as supplied for class. Their inclusion does not establish that all noncompete agreements are enforceable or replace the state-law inquiry. The full citations and dated documents remain available in the source reader.
